business_scope.primary_industry_name: Maritime Seafarer Staffing and Vessel Crew Management Agency

Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA, provisionally applied 21 September 2017)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 (PCMLTFA) and Regulations; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, Part II.1 (terrorist financing and listed entities); Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17 (SEMA) and regulations; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2011, c 24 (CJFOA); Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2011, c 23; United Nations Act, SC 1991, c 13 (UN suppression of terrorism regulations); Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9 (ABCA), Part 12.1 Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) register (enacted by SA 2022, c 25, in force 13 June 2024); FINTRAC interpretive guidance and sanctions screening directives; Transport Canada Marine Personnel Regulations under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001, SC 2001, c 26 and Maritime Labour Convention, 2006 implementation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Certificate of Incorporation (Alberta ULC) with apostille for foreign banking, KYC and counterparty verification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Alberta Corporate Registry (Director under ABCA, RSA 2000, c B-9)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention (1961) - issued by Alberta Justice and Solicitor General Authentication and Apostille Services (Canada accession effective 11 January 2024); consular legalization only for non-Convention destination states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized ISC (Individuals with Significant Control) Beneficial Ownership Register extract
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: ULC corporate secretary / registered office agent, attested by an Alberta Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for Convention destinations; sequential consular legalization (provincial authentication, Global Affairs Canada, foreign embassy) for non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized AML/KYC self-declaration and PEP/sanctions compliance certificate executed by all shareholders, directors and senior officers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Authorized signatories of the ULC, certified by an Alberta Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention states) or consular legalization chain (non-Convention states); supported by original passports, proof of address and source-of-funds documentation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-clearance screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, shareholders and senior managers against the OFAC SDN list, UN Consolidated List, Global Affairs Canada SEMA/CJFOA sanctions lists, Criminal Code Part II.1 and the UN Act terrorist entity lists, plus FATF jurisdiction watchlists and adverse-media checks; PEP identification is mandatory at the 25% beneficial-ownership threshold with enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons; screening must be refreshed every 90 days or upon any material ownership change; where the ULC administers multi-currency ship-crew payroll remittances, the entity must also assess FINTRAC money-services-business registration eligibility and apply FINTRAC record-keeping, reporting and compliance-regime obligations under PCMLTFA.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) via NUANS - Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search, filed electronically through authorized Alberta Registry Agents and the Corporate Registry online portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English is the sole operational registry language for Alberta corporations; all corporate names must be expressed in Roman-script letters; French-language names are permitted where bilingual 'Canada' or 'Alberta' usage applies, but NUANS indexing and the statutory record are in Roman characters; any non-Latin script (Cyrillic, CJK, Arabic, etc.) must be transliterated into Roman characters for the NUANS search and statutory filing; an Alberta ULC must carry the mandatory legal element 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' or the abbreviation 'ULC', with the French equivalent 'Societe a responsabilite illimitee' / 'SRI' accepted for bilingual names; numerals and punctuation are restricted to NUANS-recognized indexed formats.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: BANK / TRUST / TRUSTEE / LOAN AND INVESTMENT - restricted financial-services tokens requiring federal and/or provincial financial regulator authorization
INSURANCE / ASSURANCE - restricted tokens requiring insurance-regulator licensing
ROYAL / GOVERNMENT / CANADA / ALBERTA / MUNICIPAL - Crown-implication tokens requiring ministerial consent
CO-OPERATIVE / CONDOMINIUM - tokens reserved to entities incorporated under the applicable special statutory regimes
COLLEGE / INSTITUTE / UNIVERSITY / CHARTERED / ACCREDITED - post-secondary and professional-association consent required
ARCHITECT / ENGINEER / LAWYER / BARRISTER / SOLICITOR / NOTARY - reserved professional titles requiring regulatory-body consent
HOSPITAL / POLICE / MOUNTIE / RCMP - protected public-service marks requiring institutional or Crown consent

Words contrary to public interest, obscenity, or deceptive similarity to an existing Alberta, extra-provincial, or Canadian federal corporate name or registered trademark (prohibited under ABCA ss. 12-13 and NUANS mark-up doctrine)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In Alberta, the NUANS name-search report itself constitutes the statutory reservation and is valid for 90 days from the search date; no paid extension is available, and upon expiry the applicant must commission a fresh NUANS search. If the Director of Corporate Registry refuses a proposed name under ABCA s. 12(4), counsel shall (i) obtain written refusal reasons; (ii) file a formal reconsideration request with the Director attaching a fresh NUANS report, written consents from any existing name-holders or professional regulators, and a legal memorandum on distinguishability; (iii) if the reconsideration is denied, apply for judicial review in the Court of King's Bench of Alberta within the applicable limitation window under the Judicature Act, RSA 2000, c J-2 and the Administrative Procedures and Jurisdiction Act, SA 2008, c A-2.5; (iv) concurrently reserve a fallback distinctive-name NUANS search to preserve incorporation timelines and commercial momentum.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible with material limitations: ABCA requires every ULC to maintain a registered office located in Alberta at a real, physical street address (a P.O. Box is prohibited); a third-party registered-agency suite or serviced physical address satisfies the corporate registry formality. However, for a licensed maritime seafarer staffing and vessel crew-management agency processing multi-currency payroll, Transport Canada and Maritime Labour Convention, 2006 oversight expect physical or securely hosted personnel records, seafarer employment agreements, placement and payroll audit trails; reliance on a pure virtual mail-forwarding address is contractually possible for registry purposes but elevates commercial-substance challenge and inspection risk and may impair the issuance of Transport Canada-compliant crew documentation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-Medium, quantified at approximately 12-18% in the first twelve months: the Alberta Corporate Registry rarely conducts unannounced physical inspections of a passive ULC at incorporation; however, Transport Canada inspectors under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001, Service Canada program auditors, and Canada Revenue Agency compliance officers may perform on-site or production-order examinations of payroll, seafarer contracts, placement records, MLC 2006 evidence, and beneficial-ownership registers, particularly where the entity administers multi-currency crew wages or holds seafarer recruitment and placement mandates.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9 (ABCA), Part 2 (ss. 12–24), including ss. 12, 22(1), and 24(1) for articles and issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation; s. 101 (registered office); s. 102 (notice of directors); and corporate governance provisions in ss. 119 and 243. The unlimited liability share structure is established through the permissive share-liability clauses available to Alberta corporations qualifying as Unlimited Liability Corporations (ULC) for cross-border tax pass-through purposes.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Corporate Registry Online; filings also accepted through authorized Alberta Registries agents or legal counsel).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form COR-01 Articles of Incorporation, accompanied by the NUANS Name Reservation Certificate and Director Consent forms; issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation by the Alberta Corporate Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement applies to an Alberta ULC under the ABCA. The Articles may be filed with nominal capital; initial subscribers must accept and fund the share subscription at a stated consideration (e.g., CAD $1.00 per share) on board approval. No capital verification filing or escrow deposit is mandated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED: 1. The Articles of Incorporation filed under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) are ratified and adopted. 2. The subscription offer for 1,000 unlimited liability shares at CAD $1.00 per share is accepted; shares are allotted to subscribers for cash at par. 3. The registered office is established at [Address], Alberta, and [Corporate Services Inc.] is appointed registered agent. 4. The individuals named in the Articles are appointed first directors of the Corporation. 5. [Name] is appointed President and [Name] Secretary-Treasurer, each with signing authority. 6. Corporate bank accounts, the corporate seal, minute books, and Canada Revenue Agency business number registrations are authorized.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — NUANS Name Reservation Portal (administered by Service Alberta)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search and reservation request with up to three proposed corporate names. Each proposed name must include a legal element such as 'Unlimited Liability Company' or the abbreviation 'ULC'. The registry will return a NUANS Name Reservation Certificate, which is valid for 90 days and must accompany the Articles of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Completed NUANS search and reservation application form
Proposed corporate names in order of preference
Identification and contact details of incorporation subscribers
Supporting explanation if the name contains regulated or distinctive words
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for confusion, prohibited wording, or insufficient distinctiveness, file a fresh reservation request with an amended name list. There is no formal appeal; the applicant may reapply immediately without prejudice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) — Corporate Registry Online or in-person submission through an authorized registry agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and execute Form COR-01 Articles of Incorporation in accordance with ABCA ss. 12 and 22(1). The Articles must specify the unlimited liability share class, the first directors, the registered office address, and any restrictions on business activities. Submit the signed Articles with the NUANS certificate and prescribed filing fee; the Certificate of Incorporation is issued upon rejection-free processing.
required_dossiers: Signed Form COR-01 Articles of Incorporation
NUANS Name Reservation Certificate
Consent to Act as Director forms for each named first director
Filing fee payment confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a deficiency or rejection notice, respond in writing within the stated cure period (typically 60 days). Correct the identified defects, execute revised Articles where required, and re-file; expedited correction is available for minor typographical deficiencies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office Adoption and Agent Designation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) — Post-Incorporation Filing Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the registered office is a physical street address in Alberta, not a post-office box, and that service of process will be accepted at that address. If the address was not fully stated in the Articles, file the Notice of Registered Office and designate a local registered agent or authorized service representative for ongoing statutory correspondence.
required_dossiers: Notice of Registered Office (if not stated in Articles)
Consent of registered agent or service representative
Certified copy of Certificate of Incorporation
Directors' confirmation of physical premises availability
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry rejects a non-physical or incomplete address, file an amended Notice with the correct street address and civic particulars. Failure to maintain a physical Alberta registered office may result in administrative dissolution; remedy by immediate corrective filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance — First Board Resolutions and Statutory Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and Corporate Secretary (internal corporate act; notarization not required under the ABCA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or execute a written first board resolution in accordance with ABCA s. 119 and s. 243. Adopt the pro-forma resolution ratifying the Articles, approving the share subscription and allotment, establishing the registered office, appointing officers, and authorizing banking arrangements. Prepare the corporate minute book, share certificates, securities register, directors' register, and registered office records; retain all records at the Alberta record office.
required_dossiers: Adopted pro-forma first board resolution
Unlimited liability share certificates
Securities register and members register
Corporate minute book and corporate seal (if used)
Register of directors and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any omission in the statutory records may be cured by a supplemental directors' resolution; no registry filing is required for internal records. In the case of lost or defective share certificates, issue replacement certificates after recording a board resolution and obtaining an indemnity if necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online (BRO); Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration (TRA) for provincial corporate income tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Alberta ULC for a federal Business Number (BN) and applicable program accounts: corporate income tax (RC account), GST/HST (RT account), and payroll source deductions (RP account). Register for Alberta provincial corporate income tax with TRA. Note that although the ULC may qualify for U.S. tax pass-through treatment, under the Canadian Income Tax Act it remains a taxable entity filing a T2 corporation income tax return.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Registered office and mailing address details
Directors' names, addresses, and social insurance numbers or equivalent identifiers
Banking details for payroll remittances
Estimated annual revenue for GST/HST registration thresholds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Incomplete or incorrect registration may be corrected through the CRA My Business Account portal or by contacting the Business Registration Tele-Service. Late resolution of payroll registration may trigger penalties under the Income Tax Regulations; otherwise the registration process is administrative and generally curable within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Ministry of Jobs, Economy and Trade — Employment Agency Licensing Unit (Consumer and Business Services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an employment agency licence application covering the marine crew recruitment and crewing management services, since the business will derive remuneration from placing or supplying seafarers to vessel operators. The licence application must identify the applicant corporation, its operators, and the physical place of business in Alberta, and demonstrate compliance with Alberta employment placement fee restrictions. Maintain the licence at the registered office and file renewals as prescribed.
required_dossiers: Alberta Employment Agency Licence application form
Certified copy of Certificate of Incorporation
Corporation good-standing certificate from Alberta Corporate Registry
Proof of commercial premises in Alberta (lease or ownership document)
Operator identification and criminal record check (if required)
Insurance or bond documentation evidencing financial responsibility
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or refused, respond to the licensing officer's information request within the stated deadline. A refusal may be appealed to the appropriate Alberta administrative tribunal or court, and the application may be amended and resubmitted where the defect is procedural or evidentiary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Maritime Sector Compliance and Foreign Seafarer Placement Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Transport Canada — Marine Safety Directorate (Marine Personnel Regulations, SOR/2007-115); Employment and Social Development Canada (ESDC) — Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA) Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that all crew placements comply with the Canada Shipping Act, 2001 and applicable Marine Personnel Regulations regarding seafarer certificates, employment agreements, and vessel manning requirements. For placement of non-Canadian seafarers, obtain an approved LMIA and ensure the seafarer holds a valid Canadian work permit under the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations. Maintain complete placement records identifying the vessel, shipowner, flag state, seafarer certifications, and wage contracts for inspection by Transport Canada and employment standards authorities.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and employment agency licence
Draft seafarer employment agreements and collective agreements (if applicable)
Seafarer certificates and flag-state registration documents
Transport Canada deficiency correspondence or inspection records (where issued)
LMIA applications and work permit records for foreign seafarers
Vessel operator manning schedules and crewing requests
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: LMIA refusals may be reapplied after correcting wage, recruitment, or advertising evidence; a negative LMIA decision is not an absolute bar where the Canadian recruitment effort is demonstrably insufficient. Transport Canada deficiency letters must be remedied within the regulatory deadline, and employment standards complaints may be resolved through prescribed mediation channels.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Ministry of Jobs, Economy and Trade — Employment Agency Licensing Unit; municipal business licensing authorities in the operating municipality (e.g., Calgary or Edmonton Business Licence) as applicable
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Alberta Employment Agency Business Licence (mandatory for remuneration-based marine crew recruitment and crewing management) together with the applicable municipal business licence for the registered office premises

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA) — Environmental Assessment Program, with federal liaison through the Impact Assessment Agency of Canada if an activity is otherwise triggered
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 4 — Exempt: office-based ship crew recruitment and crew management agency activity; no physical industrial construction, no regulated discharge, and no mandatory Environmental Impact Assessment report under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act (Alberta) or the federal Impact Assessment Act, 2019
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable at operational level for vessel-manning services; the licensed agency premises must comply with municipal wastewater discharge standards for office sanitary sewage, Alberta Indoor Air Quality and Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) Code thresholds for volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and carbon dioxide, and any regulated waste handling must use certified waste carriers. As a vessel-crew placement intermediary, the agency bears no ship-source discharge liabilities; those remain with the shipowner and flag state.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for the commercial office/dispatch facility in accordance with the Alberta Fire Code; OHS Code 2009 workplace hazard assessment, first aid, emergency evacuation, and workplace violence prevention clearance; structural load inspection certified for the registered office premises; municipal property and building code compliance clearance for employee occupancy.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency / Agence du revenu du Canada; registration and filing portals are Business Registration Online, GST/HST NETFILE, and My Business Account. Alberta corporate income tax is administered by CRA under the Alberta Tax Collection Agreement, so no separate Alberta tax authority account is required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: An Alberta ULC must first complete Alberta incorporation. CRA then issues the federal Business Number (BN), a 9-digit statutory TIN. A foreign-owned ULC applies through Form RC1 or RC1-W for non-resident applicants, or through Business Registration Online, supplying the certificate or articles of incorporation, registered-office address, director information, ISIC 5222 business description, and Canadian agent contact details. The applicant selects program accounts: RC for corporate income tax, RT for GST/HST, RP for payroll, and RM for import or export accounts. GST/HST registration is effected by adding an RT program account, and the GST/HST ID is the BN followed by RT0001. If the ULC is a small supplier, RT registration is not required until the threshold is exceeded. Alberta corporate income tax does not require a separate account; CRA computes it on the T2 corporate income tax return.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no domestic check-the-box or elective pass-through regime; for Canadian Income Tax Act purposes, the Alberta ULC is a taxable Canadian corporation under subsection 250(4) and is subject to Part I tax at the entity level. The pass-through eligibility of the ULC is a foreign classification feature: under Treasury Regulation section 301.7701-3, the ULC is a foreign eligible entity and, because shareholders do not have limited liability, it is classified by default as a partnership or disregarded entity unless Form 8832 is filed to elect classification as an association taxable as a corporation. Hybrid mismatch rules in sections 18.2 and 18.3 of the Income Tax Act may restrict deductions arising from such hybrid arrangements. No GST/HST entity classification election is available; GST/HST status follows the supply activity and not the ULC share structure.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) / Harmonized Sales Tax (HST); Alberta applies only the federal 5% GST because Alberta has no provincial sales tax and no HST provincial component.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies in a single calendar quarter or in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; exceeding this small-supplier threshold creates a mandatory GST/HST registration obligation for the Alberta ULC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or government e-invoicing clearance for GST/HST. Registrants must file returns electronically via GST/HST NETFILE and remit payments by approved electronic banking channels; invoices and supporting records must be retained in Canada, generally for six years, and CRA may request commercial documents, contracts, and bank statements to verify zero-rated exports.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under Excise Tax Act Schedule VI Part V. For the crew-recruitment agency, a supply to a non-resident shipowner or foreign manning company of seafarer sourcing, vetting, placement, or payroll-administration services is zero-rated if the service is performed in Canada and is not in respect of real property situated in Canada or tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time of performance. If the service is performed entirely outside Canada, it is outside the scope of GST/HST rather than zero-rated. The supplier must be a GST/HST registrant, the recipient must be a non-resident, and the performance must be documented. Input tax credits attributable to zero-rated exports remain fully recoverable, so the business can claim a net refund of Canadian GST paid on inputs.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A / Canada Border Services Agency export report or E-export transaction number) for goods; not applicable to pure service supplies
Contract or purchase order with the non-resident shipowner or manning company clearly identifying the offshore crew services and place of performance
Commercial invoice describing the zero-rated services and showing no GST/HST charged
Bill of lading or equivalent vessel and crew deployment evidence when the service relates to an ocean-going ship
Inward remittance certificate, SWIFT credit, or bank payment advice proving receipt of export proceeds from outside Canada
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audits export claims under the GST/HST memoranda and may deny zero-rating if the documentary bundle is incomplete or the recipient or place of performance is not established. The denial exposes the ULC to a retroactive assessment of 5% GST/HST on the full consideration, compound daily interest, and, in cases of false statements or gross negligence, civil penalties and possible criminal prosecution. The normal reassessment window is four years from the filing due date; it becomes unlimited if the claim was made under misrepresentation attributable to neglect, carelessness, wilful default, or fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); foreign exchange administration is conducted under the authority of the Minister of Finance, with anti-money laundering supervision by FINTRAC and payment system oversight by the Bank of Canada under the Payment, Clearing and Settlement Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is a freely convertible floating currency with no general exchange controls on current or capital account transactions. However, cross-border transfers of CAD 10,000 or more must be reported to FINTRAC by financial intermediaries under PCMLTFA Part I. Non-resident dividend remittances are subject to Part XIII withholding tax of 25%, reduced by treaty. Profit repatriation by a ULC is unrestricted subject to corporate solvency tests and adequate supporting documentation demonstrating arm's-length transactions and economic substance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion rules applicable to Canadian-resident corporations. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency. Canadian resident exporters must report earnings to the Canada Revenue Agency, and cross-border business transactions over CAD 10,000 in value must be reported for FINTRAC purposes, but no FX conversion is mandated.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Payoneer, WorldFirst, Airwallex) are feasible as supplementary cross-border collection and crew-disbursement rails, but their primary use is Medium viability. They must not replace a Canadian chartered bank account because unlicensed EMI operations are not eligible for CDIC deposit insurance, are not directly supervised by OSFI, and may be constrained under the Retail Payment Activities Act if they cause clearing on Canadian rails. The ULC should maintain a domestic Schedule-I bank account as the treasury spine and use EMI accounts only for niche currency corridors or settlement in jurisdictions with restricted banking access.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory requirement exists for every director to appear physically at a Canadian bank branch. Tier-1 banks support remote onboarding through video consultation, liveness verification, and notarized certified true copies. A Canada-based authorized signing officer or an in-country branch meeting may be required where the ULC's directors are all non-residents and the entity is a newly incorporated unlimited liability corporation with unusual ownership structures. For a low-risk ISIC 5222 agency, remote KYC combined with registered-office address verification and Alberta registry searches is generally accepted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High aggregate payroll and payout velocity to multiple foreign crew members, creating mule-account risk flags on the ULC's bank profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Crew employment agreements (signed, dated, with passport and seafarer book copies), vessel agency contracts or MOUs with shipowners, crew identity documents (Seaman's Book/Passport), payroll ledger with complete disbursement schedule, bank pre-notification of bulk payroll runs, and an AML/CTF Beneficiary Due Diligence policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the low-risk ISIC classification and unrestricted cross-border flows without documentary trade basis.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta Corporate Access registry print and ULC formation documents, statutory operating licence for the crew recruitment agency, commercial invoices into arm's-length vessel owners, and a transaction advisory or brokerage agreement evidencing the economic purpose of each cross-border payment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained use of third-party payments (e.g., P&I club remittances, liner company commission splits) inconsistent with a simple agency model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed flow-of-funds diagram, escrow/trust account structure if client funds are held, signed sub-agency commission agreements, KYC/CIP on every counterparty, and corporate resolution authorising the ULC to hold funds on behalf of vessel principals.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from foreign shareholders into the Alberta ULC are executed over SWIFT with an MT103 using purpose code 'B1' (Capital Subscription) or 'C11' depending on the bank's tag 23B mapping. The wire must reference the ULC's Alberta Corporate Registry number and comply with FINTRAC electronic funds transfer reporting at the CAD 10,000 threshold. Route via a Canadian correspondent in Toronto/Vancouver and clear the instruction as 'EQUITY CONTRIBUTION / CAPITAL INJECTION'. If the share capital is held in a foreign currency, the receiving bank can credit a foreign-currency account without conversion; if CAD is required, conversion occurs at the bank's corporate mid-rate plus 0.10% to 0.20% FX spread.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary outbound rail for crew wages and trade settlements is SWIFT MT103 for direct bank-to-bank credits to beneficiaries in their home jurisdictions. For higher-value ship-supply settlements, a Commercial Letter of Credit (UCP600) issued by a Canadian chartered bank is used, with documentary collection (URC522) as an alternative for established counterparties. Domestic CAD outbound payments above $25 million (or time-critical smaller amounts) clear through Payments Canada Lynx; multi-currency payouts follow SWIFT/CHIPS/Fedwire corridors. All outbound transfers are queued for FINTRAC EFT reporting and must carry a reference to the underlying crew contract or invoice.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards for CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, CAD/GBP and CAD/JPY with a Schedule-I chartered bank
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies with no onshore deliverable market or bilateral convertibility restrictions (e.g., CNY, IDR, BDT), executed through an OSFI-authorised dealer
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for long-dated rebalancing of crew payroll currency exposures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days of the corporation's incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 100 applies after the 60-day window; continued default for one full year may lead to administrative dissolution of the ULC.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month up to 12 months; continuing non-compliance may result in criminal charges and certificate of default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months of the fiscal year end for annual filers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 4% late remittance penalty plus 1% per month (up to 4 months); interest on unpaid amounts accrues daily.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, a distributing corporation must appoint an independent auditor. A non-distributing private ULC may dispense with the auditor each year by unanimous shareholders' resolution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted by the Canadian Accounting Standards Board, or Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) where eligible.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta does not yet impose a separate UBO annual filing for provincial ULCs. The annual return updates registered office, director list, and issued share capital. In-house share transfer registers and annual director confirmations must record any shareholder/UBO changes and be retained at the registered office.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 - 5,000 if audit waived; USD 5,000 - 12,000 for full audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined general corporate rate (Federal Base Part I rate 15% under ITA s.123(1)(a) plus Alberta general corporate income tax 8%). Applicable to a non-resident-owned Alberta ULC that is not a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday or preferential sectoral rate for maritime seafarer staffing in Canada or Alberta. If the ULC is Canadian-controlled and qualifies as a CCPC, a combined 11% rate applies to the first C$500,000 of active business income (federal 9% + Alberta 2%). Federal SR&ED provides a 15% non-refundable credit for a non-CCPC ULC (35% refundable for a CCPC). Alberta imposes no general capital tax for this activity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (including Alberta's corporate tax, administered by the Canada Revenue Agency under a single tax collection agreement; no separate Alberta AT1 return is required). Filing portal: CRA Corporation Internet Filing / approved EFILE commercial software; mandatory electronic filing where the corporation's gross revenue exceeds C$1,000,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual T2 return; quarterly instalment obligations during the year for current taxes, with instalments due on the last day of each month or quarter depending on entity size and timing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline: within six months after the fiscal year-end (ITA s.150(1)). Balance-due day: two months after the fiscal year-end for a non-CCPC ULC (ITA s.157(1)(a)); three months where the corporation is a CCPC with taxable income within the small-business limit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Corporate identity panel and provincial jurisdiction boxes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Alberta jurisdiction, ULC statutory designation, business number, industry code (NAICS 488390), ultimate parent name and country of residence.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose the U.S. sole shareholder and its jurisdiction; do not tick the CCPC box unless the corporation is actually Canadian-controlled; show Alberta address and board of directors' location for treaty-treaty determination.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from ship-crew recruitment, crewing-management contracts and payroll-administration fees, converted to Canadian dollars; include all Swift-wire and multi-currency receipts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shipowner clients chargebacks must be recorded at arm's-length invoice amounts; any offshore revenue derived through a Canadian permanent establishment remains fully taxable in Canada.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Crew wages and salaries, CPP/EI employer contributions, marine insurance, visa and medical-certificate costs, travel, rent, professional fees, and capital cost allowance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductibility requires contemporaneous third-party records; management fees paid to a non-resident parent must satisfy ITA s.247 arm's-length standard or be added back.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after Schedule 1 adjustments, loss carryforwards, and charitable/dividend deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply non-capital loss carryforwards limited to 20 years forward and 3 years backward; capital losses are deductible only against capital gains.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 400 and Schedule 5 - Federal Part I tax computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal base tax at 15% on taxable income, with applicable foreign tax credits and SR&ED investment tax credits netted against tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-owned ULC cannot claim the small-business deduction; ensure foreign tax credits attach to foreign source business or non-business income only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Alberta corporate income tax at 8% on taxable income allocated to Alberta; computation integrated into the T2 and E-filing engine.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Alberta tax follows the federal allocation; no separate provincial return is due, and no Alberta branch-tax extension applies to corporate income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Attachments: Form T106, NR4 and T1134
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: T106 (Information Return on non-arm's-length transactions with non-residents), NR4 (payments to non-residents), and T1134 (foreign affiliate disclosures) accompany the T2 where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: T106 must report all intercompany transactions in Canadian-dollar equivalents; NR4 and remittance forms capture Part XIII withholding on dividends, interest and royalties paid to the U.S. parent.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% of the balance payable plus 1% per full month (max 12 months). Repeat failure: 10% plus 2% per full month (max 20 months). Late balance: prescribed-rate interest compounded daily. Additional non-filing penalties for Form T106 (C$100 per day, max C$2,500; escalated to C$25,000 for repeat failures). Full Part XIII withholding and transfer-pricing penalties remain separately assessable.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (ITA s.212(2)) on dividends paid by the Alberta ULC to its non-resident shareholder.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Under the Canada-US Income Tax Convention (as amended by the 1997 Protocol), the U.S.-resident beneficial owner corporation that directly owns at least 10% of the ULC's voting stock is entitled to a 5% dividend withholding rate (all other U.S. residents: 15%). Procedure: before each dividend payment the U.S. shareholder must provide the ULC with a valid IRS Form 6166 (U.S. Certificate of Residence, i.e., the functional U.S. TRC) and a complete Form W-8BEN-E; the ULC may then reduce the 25% Part XIII withholding at source to the treaty rate. Where excess withholding is applied, the U.S. shareholder files CRA Form NR7-R for a refund within two years after the end of the calendar year in which the tax was withheld. The treaty exemption/reduced rate is not automatic: the parties must update the W-8BEN-E every three years and on any material ownership change.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory Part XIII rate 25% (ITA s.212(1)(d)); treaty rate 0% for royalties paid to a U.S. resident under the Canada-US DTA as amended by the 1997 Protocol (grandfathered film agreements are the principal exception). Interest: statutory Part XIII rate 25% (ITA s.212(1)(b)); treaty rate 0% for arm's-length interest to a U.S. resident, subject to an anti-abuse limitation where the interest is disproportionate to the payer's equity or where debt has participating, profit-contingent or recharacterized-dividend features; excessive related-party interest may be recharacterized as a dividend and bear the 25% statutory rate or 5% treaty rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Canada has no statutory revenue threshold for transfer-pricing documentation: each cross-border transaction with a non-resident related party is subject to contemporaneous documentation under ITA s.247(4) (prepared at or before the filing deadline for the ULC's taxation year). The s.247(3) penalty applies only where the aggregate transfer-pricing adjustment exceeds the lesser of C$5,000,000 and 10% of the ULC's gross revenue for the year. Canada's Country-by-Country reporting threshold is C$750 million (or EUR 750 million) in consolidated group revenue of the ultimate parent; below that threshold, CRA nonetheless expects OECD-compliant Local File/Master File standard documentation as articulated in Information Circular IC 87-2R.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) are not in force in Canada or Alberta. The ULC remains a fully taxable Canadian corporation regardless of its U.S. 'disregarded entity' tax election. The relevant substance-requirements are the GAAR (ITA s.245), the section 247 transfer-pricing recharacterization, statutory anti-hybrid and anti-conduit rules, and the principle that a ULC must maintain real Canadian substance (Alberta registered office, active crew-placement management, Canadian bank accounts, Canadian directors' meetings, payroll and payroll records maintained in Canada) to support treaty benefits and avoid a sham or factual-authority reassessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Criminal tax evasion - marine crew payroll and placement-fee fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilful omission of Swift-wire placement commissions paid by shipowners into foreign bank accounts, fabrication of seafarer employment records, or destruction of crew-file vouchers to understate taxable income of the ULC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ITA s.239(1): on indictment, a fine of not less than 50% and not more than 200% of the tax sought to be evaded plus imprisonment for up to 5 years; on summary conviction, C$2,000 to C$100,000 fine and up to 2 years imprisonment. Civil gross-negligence penalty under ITA s.163(2) of 50% of the understated tax. The normal four-year reassessment window is suspended indefinitely for misrepresentation (ITA s.152(4)(a)(i)).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who directed or acquiesced in the fraudulent filings are personally exposed in the ULC's unlimited-liability structure; the CRA can pursue director assets directly. Criminal arrest warrants, seizure of personal bank accounts, travel restrictions and bail conditions barring international departures (including for non-resident U.S. directors) apply; upon conviction, imprisonment to 5 years is available.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Alberta ULC purely as an invoicing buffer with no Canadian crew-placement staff, no local management, and no substantive contracts, while the net margin is distributed to a non-resident parent that performs all real work.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR (ITA s.245(2)) denies the tax benefit; the CRA may re-derive the ULC's taxable income under s.152(7), assess 50% gross-negligence penalties under s.163(2), and disallow refunds. In flagrant cases the ULC's files may be referred to the Public Prosecution Service of Canada for s.239 charges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Because a ULC has no capital shield, shareholders and directors face direct contractual and CRA claims; courts may treat deliberate asset stripping as a fraudulent conveyance and order civil restitution, injunctions freezing personal assets, and, for non-resident directors, removal under immigration enforcement measures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to remit Part XIII withholding on dividends and Treaty form abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Declaring and paying dividends, royalty or interest to the U.S. parent without withholding 25%, or applying the 5% treaty rate without holding a valid IRS Form 6166 and Form W-8BEN-E.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ITA s.227(8): penalty of 10% of the unwithheld amount (20% where the failure continues) plus prescribed daily interest. Knowingly failing to remit is criminal under s.227(9): up to 200% of the tax and 5 years imprisonment. The ULC is also assessed for the withheld amounts as principal payer.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable under ITA s.227.1 for the full unremitted Part XIII tax, interest and penalty. The CRA can issue civil execution against director assets without first exhausting the ULC; travel monitoring and restraint orders are available in enforcement proceedings where evasion is alleged.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing mispricing of crewing-management fees
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Billing shipowner clients at below-cost commission rates while the non-resident related entity overcharges for marketing or management services; or failing to prepare contemporaneous section 247 documentation and pricing irrelevant to the commercial risk profile of the agency.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ITA s.247(2) re-determination of the arm's-length price and income; s.247(3) penalty of 10% of the net transfer-pricing adjustment where the aggregate adjustment exceeds the lesser of C$5,000,000 and 10% of gross revenue and contemporaneous documentation is absent. Recharacterized amounts may be treated as disguised dividends subject to Part XIII 25% withholding (or 5% under treaty).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve falsified intercompany contracts may face gross-negligence penalties; indemnity from the ULC is unenforceable in the ULC's unlimited-liability structure, and personal liability can be pursued through s.227.1 for associated withholding failures or through civil actions for breach of fiduciary duty.
